messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate detected on canary for service=redwood-inference-api region=eu-west-1. 5xx rate 12% in last 2m, baseline 0.3%. Pager: #eng-oncall.
ashley_oncall: ack. I'm looking at canary cluster metrics and recent deploys. pulling up kitchen logs.
sam_dev: I pushed canary 2026-03-15T02:45Z — small config override to token_bucket and a new feature flag rollout (ff:model-prefetch-v2=true). not aware of anything that should cause 5xxs but will standby.
ashley_oncall: dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/canary-overview
ashley_oncall: top symptoms: increased p99 latency, spike in gRPC CLOSED status, errors in kv-cache init during first requests. quick log sample:
```
2026-03-15T02:46:10Z service inference-kanary-3 module runtime ERROR "KV cache failed to init: mismatched schema v1 vs v2"
2026-03-15T02:46:10Z service inference-kanary-3 module handler WARN "fallback to uncached path"
2026-03-15T02:46:11Z service inference-kanary-3 module transport ERROR "grpc: upstream returned status=UNAVAILABLE"
```
ashley_oncall: Looks like config/schema mismatch. Could be that ff:model-prefetch-v2 toggled a code path expecting a different cache schema.
sam_dev: confirmed — the flag flips an initialization path that expects new cache schema. I forgot to include a migration step in the rollout. my bad. we should kill the flag immediately.
maya_sre: @ashley_oncall, @sam_dev — agree. Flip the kill switch for ff:model-prefetch-v2 in prod canary and pause the rollout. If flipping doesn't drop 5xxs in 2 minutes, initiate canary rollback.
ashley_oncall: executing kill switch via flags service.
ashley_oncall: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/model-prefetch-v2/kill -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -d '{"scope":"canary"}'`
deploy-bot: Flag change queued: model-prefetch-v2 scope=canary action=kill requested_by=ashley_oncall id=ff-98765
deploy-bot: Flag change applied: model-prefetch-v2 scope=canary action=kill by=ashley_oncall at=2026-03-15T02:48:05Z
ashley_oncall: applied. Monitoring metrics.
ashley_oncall: 60s after kill: 5xx rate down to 4.1%, p99 latency improving.
ashley_oncall: 3m after kill: 5xx rate 0.6% — trending to baseline. looks like killing flag resolved primary failure mode.
sam_dev: i'll open a changelist to add migration + safety check and re-run canary with stricter rollout (10% -> 30% steps) once validated.
maya_sre: good. we still need a short incident record and customer-impact assessment. @lina_pm can you capture user-visible impact?
lina_pm: checking upstream SLO impact. Affected requests were primarily prefetch/batch warmup calls from hosted customers in eu-west. Preliminary tally: ~0.8% of production requests in eu-west experienced 5xx within the 8m window. No broad customer-side errors reported via support yet. notifying CS to watch for spikes. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4621
ashley_oncall: posting incident summary to #incidents and marking canary as paused. will handoff to maya for postmortem if you can drive next steps.
maya_sre: taking handoff. next actions: 1) confirm canary stability for 30m 2) require migration in changelist + unit tests for cache schema 3) update rollout plan to include migration window and feature-flag gating 4) postmortem draft with timeline + RCA.
ashley_oncall: handing off. summary:
- issue: feature-flag enabled new prefetch path with schema v2 but no migration -> kv-cache init errors -> increased 5xxs in canary
- mitigation: killed ff:model-prefetch-v2 in canary at 1767009885 (2:48:05Z), canary paused
- impact: eu-west canary 0.8% request failure during 02:46–02:54Z window, no major customer escalations yet
- owner: maya_sre for postmortem, sam_dev for changelist
ashley_oncall: handing off to @maya_sre (oncall -> incident owner). paging off for me.
maya_sre: acknowledged. @aaron_ops please check if any automated billing/alerting runs ingested failed requests; ensure downstream telemetry pipelines didn't truncate.
aaron_ops: on it. running a quick query now. if anything looks off i'll flag.
aaron_ops: telemetry check: ingestion lag small, no lost events detected. will follow up in postmortem.
lina_pm: will coordinate CS message if any customers reach out; drafting a short factual note.
maya_sre: thanks everyone. I'll own the postmortem + mitigation tasks. leaving canary paused until migration + tests merged. closing pager for now — monitor for 30m.
incident-bot: Pager resolved by maya_sre at 1767010499. Incident status: mitigated (canary paused, flag killed).
